finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
Deserialized object is inspected and returned, which can also trigger gadget methods and leak output

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, signature/HMAC, class allowlist, or input validation exists. Sinatra has no built-in protection for this; no before filters in the file. The only file in the repo is app.rb.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-7 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing params[:state] through Base64.decode64 straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, with no auth, before filter, signature check or class allowlist anywhere in the single-file repo.
